newsitem.title: UK: Grain buyers want more origin data, farmers told.
newsitem.headline: Grain buyers want more origin data, farmers told.

text.p: Grains buyers need increasingly precise information on the origin and nature of their purchases, UK growers and traders have been told.
Traceability, in particular, is becoming an ever bigger issue for grain buyers, a group of them heard at a forum designed to help them tailor produce to export markets.

At the forum hosted by British Cereal Exports (BCE) on March 10, they were told that growers in the UK must tailor their choice of varieties to meet the needs of foreign buyers, BCE said in a statement released on March 17.

Antonio Rodriguez of Portuguese miller Nacional told the forum in a paper on bread and wheat flour consumption that his clients wanted to know everything about the cereals used. Currently Portugal's own wheat production accounts for less than 15 percent of the 950,000 tonnes used by its milling sector.

At present France is the biggest supplier of medium quality wheat for breadflour, with Germany supplying high protein improving wheats and Spain supplying biscuit quality flour. Occasionally Denmark supplies medium quality wheat for breadflour and the UK supplies wheat for biscuitflour and for animal feed.
"UK growers must produce consistently good quality cereals at a competitive price, Usborne Grain managing director Mike Adams told the forum.
In a rapidly changing world grains market with the needs of the customer and end-user becoming more important, cereals producers need to work with industry to compete, BCE director Alan Almond said.
This forum was the third of four being arranged by British Cereals Exports, the export promotion division of the Home Grown Cereals Authority. The final meeting will be at Salisbury on April 3.
